Research.title: Real Long-Term Memory for AI: A 50-Million-Token Window That Is Faster and Cheaper Than Recompute
Research.summary: This paper tests a KV-cache persistence layer (galahad-kv) that saves transformer key-value states to encrypted local NVMe storage and reloads them byte-exact, eliminating redundant recomputation. Evaluated at 50 million tokens via vLLM, the approach delivers meaningful latency and cost reductions for long-context workloads. Practitioners building document-heavy or session-persistent applications should consider KV caching to disk as a practical alternative to full context recompute.

Research.title: Grammar Concept Annotation at Scale: Deployed Fine-Tuned Small Language Models Outperform Prompted Frontier Models
Research.summary: Preply fine-tuned Qwen3.5 small language models on filtered teacher-generated supervision for grammar concept annotation in language-learning transcripts, and found that the deployed SLMs outperform prompted frontier models at scale. This demonstrates a cost-effective path for specialized annotation tasks: targeted fine-tuning on domain-specific data beats expensive API calls to large general models. Teams building educational or enterprise NLP pipelines should weigh fine-tuned SLMs against frontier model prompting for high-volume labeling workloads.

Research.title: Sparse Attention Is Matrix Approximation, Not Choosing from a Bag of Values
Research.summary: This paper argues that existing sparse attention methods are mathematically flawed because they select entries based on scalar magnitude rather than treating attention as a matrix approximation problem. The authors propose a corrected formulation that better preserves the full attention matrix's structure, improving efficiency without sacrificing quality. For engineers building long-context LLM inference pipelines, this reframing suggests current sparse attention heuristics may leave significant performance on the table.

Research.title: Diffu-LoRA: A Novel Low-Rank Adaptation for Personalized Diffusion Models
Research.summary: Diffu-LoRA introduces a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for text-to-image diffusion models that learns how to optimally distribute adaptation capacity across layers, rather than applying uniform LoRA rank everywhere. This addresses a key open question in personalized image generation: where to concentrate trainable parameters for best identity preservation. Product teams building image customization features on top of diffusion models may find this approach yields better results with fewer parameters than standard LoRA.

Tools.title: Let your AI agents paint big arrows, boxes and text on your screen
Tools.summary: This open-source tool lets AI agents render large visual overlays—arrows, boxes, and text—directly on the user's screen, enabling richer visual feedback loops in agentic UI automation workflows. It addresses a practical gap in computer-use agents: communicating intent or focus areas visually without modifying the underlying application. Developers building desktop automation or screen-based agents can use this as a lightweight annotation layer for debugging or user-facing guidance.

Tools.title: Introducing Falcon ASR
Tools.summary: TII (Technology Innovation Institute) has released Falcon ASR, a new automatic speech recognition model available on Hugging Face. The release extends the Falcon model family into the audio domain, giving developers an open alternative for speech-to-text tasks. Teams integrating voice interfaces into AI products now have another capable open-weight option to benchmark against existing ASR solutions.

Industry News.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for "mishandling research information"
Industry News.summary: OpenAI terminated three safety researchers, who in turn dispute the misconduct characterization and warn the firings will have a chilling effect on internal safety advocacy. The incident raises questions about how frontier AI labs balance information security with the ability of safety teams to raise concerns. For AI product builders, this highlights ongoing tensions at major AI providers that could affect the stability and direction of safety-focused model development.

Industry News.title: Claude Docs, Slides, and Design now available on all plans including Free
Industry News.summary: Anthropic has taken Claude's collaborative document, presentation, and design creation tools out of beta and made them available to all users, including free-tier accounts, with real-time co-editing between users and Claude. The move positions Anthropic more directly against Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 Copilot in the productivity suite space. Developers building on Claude APIs should note this signals Anthropic's push toward end-user productivity as a core use case alongside the API ecosystem.

Industry News.title: AI-ready biological data: $1.8B global commitment
Industry News.summary: A $1.8 billion global initiative, centered around the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub network, has been announced to create AI-ready biological datasets and infrastructure. This scale of investment signals that life sciences is becoming a primary application domain for frontier AI, with structured data availability being identified as the key bottleneck. AI product builders targeting biotech and pharma verticals should monitor this initiative as it is likely to unlock new model training opportunities and application niches.

Industry News.title: Synthesis Superintelligence: from Semiconductors to Superconductors — Periodic Labs' Liam Fedus and Ekin Dogus Cubuk
Industry News.summary: This podcast episode features Liam Fedus and Ekin Dogus Cubuk of Periodic Labs discussing AI's role in accelerating materials science discovery, from semiconductor design to superconductors. The conversation covers how AI-driven synthesis and simulation pipelines are being applied to physical science R&D. Consultants advising on AI strategy in deep tech or hardware-adjacent industries will find this a useful window into how frontier AI capabilities are being directed toward materials discovery.
